A1.justification: Both PDFs contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices for the same LaTtE-Flow work. Renamed models and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, architectural ablations, convergence measurements, and attention analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original generation experiments and ablations and adds a human preference study in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The layerwise timestep experts, residual-attention mechanism, training objectives, and cached-conditioning inference procedure are retained. Couple is renamed LaTtE-Flow, while the existing Blend architecture moves to Appendix A; neither constitutes a new method.

E1.justification: Coverage remains ImageNet generation and the same eight multimodal understanding benchmarks. The human study samples existing ImageNet class prompts and changes output assessment without introducing a new model task, domain, or input scenario.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds an explicit Qwen2-VL-2B comparator. Figure 4 removes the Vanilla Blend convergence comparison, although its final scores and the original generation comparator roster remain in Appendix A, Table 4.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds a protocol using 50 ImageNet prompts and 10 annotators, with anonymized, randomized rankings, permitted ties, and realism/semantic-accuracy criteria. TFLOPs reporting is also added. The existing ImageNet training budget, sampling settings, and automated evaluation recipe remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds human assessment and qualitative examples examining photorealism, prompt fidelity, and comparator failures. Figure 4 drops the Blend convergence curves. The group-size, residual-attention, sampling/CFG, and head-gating analyses otherwise remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new annotator sample counts and descriptive preference rates do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and ablation values remain unchanged, including FID 5.79 and 0.052 seconds/image for Couple, renamed LaTtE-Flow. New results include generation costs of 28.3 TFLOPs for Vanilla versus 7.08 for LaTtE-Flow, Table 2's backbone/compute entries, and preference wins of 71.4% against Janus Pro and 63.4% against Show-o. Blend convergence curves are removed.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 adds a cache-inclusive compute model and derives S = (K + theta)/(1 + theta), approaching K as caching overhead is amortized. This extends v1's asymptotic complexity argument; the flow-matching and residual-attention mathematics otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The conclusion changes its highlighted speedup from 'up to 48×' to 'around 6×', although Section 6.1 retains the 48× Show-o comparison. The abstract's 6× claim and the two central architectural contributions remain.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds interpretation of visual quality through photorealism and semantic fidelity, discussing attractive but misaligned Show-o outputs and structural errors in Janus Pro outputs. v2 also makes exact inheritance of backbone understanding performance explicit. The original training-duration and timestep-partitioning limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies natural-language caption conditioning for ImageNet and supplies the human annotation instructions. It removes v1's code/checkpoint access footnote, without establishing that the resources themselves became unavailable. Existing hyperparameter, hardware, and training-duration disclosures largely match.

R1.justification: v2 adds ResNet as motivation for residual connections and UniWorld as a concurrent frozen-backbone approach. The principal related-work discussion is retained; other title and publication updates refer to existing cited works.

P1.justification: Localized rewriting foregrounds Couple under the LaTtE-Flow name, moves Blend material into Appendix A, and relocates the impact statement after the conclusion. Acknowledgments and an LLM-writing disclosure are added. Most prose and the main section sequence remain.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference paper with extensive figure/table reflow. The architecture display is split between the main text and appendix, the complete generation comparison reappears as Table 4, Table 2 gains a row and compute column, and Figures 10–11 add preference bars and comparative images.

improvement.justification: The cache-aware derivation, explicit backbone comparison, and documented human study improve transparency and support for the central claims. These gains are partly offset by removal of the code/checkpoint link and Blend convergence curves, plus preference percentages totaling only 99.6% and 99.8%. Overall, the revision provides a limited net improvement in evidential clarity.
